summary: Warm Springs Reservation peak; a pole lookout from the 1930s was replaced in 1938 and lost in a 1943 forest fire. Now gone, with no site description today.

facts.design: 40-foot pole live-in tower (register) or 45-foot wooden tower (1935 report); replaced in 1938 by a 6x6 ft ground cab and tent cabin
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in a 1943 forest fire, per the register and firelookout.com; no source describes what remains

events.note: Lookout tower reported to be erected that season on Bald Peter, the first on the reservation's forests
Firelookout.com dates the first 40-foot pole live-in tower to 1933
Bald Peter lookout reported the east line apparently not holding during a large fire in the Fly Creek area
Annual forestry report says a 45-foot wooden tower on Bald Peter was completed that fall
Pole tower replaced by a 6x6 ft ground cab and tent cabin
Register says removed in a 1943 forest fire; firelookout.com says destroyed in one
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on August 16, 2010

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com describe a first 40-foot pole tower, which firelookout.com dates to 1933. A 1935 forestry report describes a 45-foot wooden tower completed that fall. The sources do not say whether these are the same tower, so both are listed as events.

notes_for_editor: Brief access 'permission' is not stated by any source read, so access is left out of facts. Brief height_m 13.7 matches the 45-foot tower in the 1935 report, not the 40-foot pole tower in the register; it was removed from facts because no source read states a height in metres. Brief elevation 2003.8 m matches the register (2,004 m). The 1925 letter's author is not named in the text read. A 2001 'Bald Peter Fire' on the reservation appeared only in search snippets and was not read, so it is not used. No staffing names are used beyond what the sources state.
